bugs.summary: C implementation of the byte code compiler, about 90x faster than compiler::cmpfun()
bugs.creator: kevinushey

comments.text:
The byte code compiler is written in R, and during package installation a substantial amount of time is spent byte-compiling the package sources. Under the JIT, the first call of each closure pays for its compilation as well.

I would like to propose a C implementation, src/main/bccompile.c: a port of cmp.R that emits instructions and constants in the same order, so the code objects are identical. The JIT, package installation and compiler::cmpfun()/compile() use it by default; R_BYTECODE_COMPILER=R or .Internal(nativeCompiler(FALSE)) selects the R implementation, which stays in the package as the reference.

Timings (macOS arm64, MAKEFLAGS=-j8): R CMD INSTALL of Matrix 1.7-6 takes 18 s instead of 29 s (its byte-compile step 3.3 s instead of 13 s) and of lattice 0.23-1 2.4 s instead of 4.3 s (0.35 s instead of 2.2 s), with the same byte code installed. bccompile-timing.R, attached, compiles the 4089 closures in base, stats, utils, methods and tools with both implementations and compares the results: 14.3 s versus 0.16 s, identical code for all of them.

Proposed patch: attached as bccompile.diff, against r90874. It includes compiler/tests/native.R, which compares the two implementations on every closure in the base packages. The cost is a second implementation to keep in step with cmp.R; that test is there to catch drift. I would understand if that maintenance burden means the patch is not wanted, but I am happy to iterate on it or expand it if there is interest.

The patch is also submitted as https://github.com/r-devel/r-svn/pull/463, where CI results can be seen.
